court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Family Court, Aurangabad in Petition No.A-67/2010 and Petition No.A-81/2011
case_name: Sainand Kashinath Dhakne vs Kalpana Sainand Dhakne
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: The husband filed a petition for dissolution of marriage or judicial separation under the Hindu Marriage Act. The wife filed a petition for restitution of conjugal rights. Both parties led evidence, and the trial court passed a common judgment.

legal_principles.principle: The court may grant divorce if the respondent's behavior is such that it endangers the life of the appellant and his family members.
legal_principles.held: There is also danger to the life of the appellant and his family members due to the acts of the respondent and they are living under fear and threats.
use_in: divorce cases where there is a threat to the life of the parties involved

legal_principles.principle: The court may grant divorce if the respondent has caused physical and mental cruelty to the appellant.
legal_principles.held: Physical and mental cruelty was caused to her.
use_in: divorce cases where there is physical and mental cruelty involved

outcome.final_order: The appeals are taken up for final disposal, and the Family Court's common judgment is set aside.
